B: Alright. Can you hear me?
A: Yes, I can hear you. Can you hear me alright?
B: Ar, you're fine. Walsall, ain't you? Darren said.
A: Yes, that's right. Leanne. You're Kelly? Ellie mentioned you.
B: Everyone's mentioning everyone. Whereabouts are you, then?
A: Erm, I live just off the Wolverhampton Road, but I work in Bloxwich. At a GP surgery, I'm a practice nurse.
B: Bloxwich? My mom's Bloxwich. Which surgery?
A: I probably shouldn't say, sorry. But it's one of the ones near the high street.
B: Fair enough. She'll be at one of them, she's always at the doctor's. She's not well, her chest, her legs, all sorts. I take her when I can, but I don't drive, so it's two buses.
A: Oh, that's a lot. Is she managing at home alright?
B: Just about. She does my school pick-ups still, for my youngest. I dunno how long she can keep that up, to be honest. I try not to think about it.
A: No, I understand. It's hard when it's your mom, isn't it. If she's got a chest thing, she might be on our asthma or COPD reviews. I run those. Sorry, that's a bit of a work answer.
B: No, it's alright. You're not what I thought, you know. I thought from your photo you'd be dead posh.
A: Posh? Me? I went to the sixth form college in Walsall. I have a chippy tea every Saturday.
B: Do you? Where from?
A: The one near me, I won't tell you which, you'll judge it. Fish, chips and a bap with the leftover chips, sometimes.
B: A chip bap, now we're talking. Mine get a chippy on payday. Or a Chinese, if it's a good month.
A: That sounds lovely. You've got children, then?
B: Two. Kai's sixteen, doing mechanics at college, never comes out his room except to empty the fridge. Ellie-Mae's eleven, won't wear her blazer. I'm a care assistant on top, so I'm shattered most of the time. What about you, have you got kids?
A: No. No, just me. I've got next door's cat sometimes, if that counts.
B: It counts. Less hassle than kids, honest.
A: Probably, yes. Erm, do you get out much, walking or anything? I go along the canal most nights.
B: I walk everywhere 'cause I don't drive. I did that Couch to 5K once. Gave up in week three.
A: Oh, I did that too! I got to the end, but I never ran again after. I think I just walk now and call it exercise.
B: See, that's better than me. Week three, I was dying. My back's gone from the hoisting anyway.
A: You want to get that looked at, you know, if it keeps on. Sorry, I'm doing it again, being a nurse.
